title: GAMMALN and GAMMALN.PRECISE publish identical bits on build 20131
upstream_status_verbatim: Extended search findings (2026-07-12) -- the published-table route is closed
status_plain: This is an Excel-versus-Excel identity check, not a pass rate. On build 20131 both surfaces resolve to the same custom Cody-family implementation and publish identical bits at every probed point. OxFunc mirrors the identity structurally: `gammaln_precise_kernel` is a one-line delegation to `gammaln_kernel`. The source publishes no numerator or denominator for the identity; the dedicated probe file holds 17 rows.

counts.source_sentence: - **`GAMMALN.PRECISE` == legacy `GAMMALN`** on modern build 20131: identical bits at every probed point, both +-3 ULP from true. Excel 2010 introduced `.PRECISE`, but on this build BOTH resolve to the SAME custom Cody-family implementation

counts.build_note: The cached rows carry excel_build 20131; the comparison itself is a computation over stored bits, not an oracle run.

counts.ambiguity_note: NOT a live-Excel measurement. It is stronger evidence for the identity than the source's own 17-row probe, but it is an agent's computation over cached bits and may not be shelved beside an oracle run.
counts.source_sentence: GAMMALN.PRECISE == GAMMALN on 109 shared cached arguments with 0 bit mismatches
